prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Pearland, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1221; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision at the intersection in Pearland. Can you state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just keep it to my first name, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were coming from and where you were headed when the accident happened?

A: I was driving home from work. I was heading through the intersection on the green light, going straight.

Q: Got it. What was the first thing you noticed about the other vehicle?

A: Honestly, I didn't see it until it was almost on me. It came from my right side and went through the red, I think. I hit the brakes but there wasn't time.

Q: Did you have a chance to swerve or stop at all?

A: Not really. I braked hard and tried to steer a little, but it hit my driver's side door.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did the airbags deploy?

A: The side curtain came out, I think. The front ones didn't.

Q: How are you feeling physically right now?

A: My neck is pretty stiff and sore. It got worse through the evening. I'm also a little tender in the shoulder.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or been to an urgent care since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same day. They said it looked like a neck strain and gave me a muscle relaxer and some instructions for stretching.

Q: Do you have any ongoing treatment scheduled?

A: I have a follow-up with my primary care doctor next week, and I'm doing physical therapy referrals if things don't improve.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about how the accident happened?

A: Just that I was driving the speed limit and I was paying attention. I'm pretty sure the other driver was at fault.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
